original_question: If f is a polynomial automorphism of C^d with dynamical degree λ(f) = 1, must the degree growth satisfy deg(f^n) ≍ n^k for some natural number k, and if k ≥ 1 must f preserve a rational fibration?
target_in_paper: Section 10.1, Question 39 (the lambda(f)=1 case inside Problem 8 on degree growth for polynomial automorphisms of C^d).
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's actual target: it matches the content of Section 10.1, Question 39 almost verbatim. In particular, you correctly identified the ambient category (polynomial automorphisms of C^d), the hypothesis lambda(f)=1, the expected polynomial degree growth deg(f^n) ~ n^k, and the follow-up question asking whether nontrivial growth (k >= 1) should force preservation of a rational fibration (Section 10.1, Question 39, p. 23).
missing_details: The paper places this in the higher-dimensional setting inherited from Problem 8, namely polynomial automorphisms of C^d with d >= 3; without saying this, the question sounds broader than the immediate paper context (Section 10.1, Problem 8, p. 23).

The dynamical degree lambda(f) should be defined explicitly as lambda(f) := lim_{n->infinity} deg(f^n)^(1/n), with existence justified by the submultiplicative inequality deg(f^(n+m)) <= deg(f^n) deg(f^m) stated immediately before Question 39 (Section 10.1, p. 23).

The degree notation should be made explicit: deg(f^n) is the polynomial degree of the n-th iterate; Section 10.1 points back to the degree convention introduced earlier in Section 6.1 (Section 6.1, p. 14; Section 10.1, p. 23).
The asymptotic notation should be unpacked: deg(f^n) ~ n^k means there exist constants c, C > 0 such that c n^k <= deg(f^n) <= C n^k for all sufficiently large n.

The phrase 'for some natural number k' is slightly ambiguous unless one specifies whether 0 is allowed; because the paper separately asks 'if k >= 1', the stand-alone version is clearer if it says 'for some integer k >= 0'.

The phrase 'preserve a rational fibration' is standard but implicit; to make the question stand-alone, one should specify that this means there exists a nonconstant dominant rational map pi: C^d -> B with 0 < dim(B) < d and a birational self-map g of B such that pi o f = g o pi.
It should be stated explicitly that this is an open question, not a theorem or conjecture already resolved in the paper.
Question 40 is only presented as a weaker related problem, not as an equivalent reformulation, so it should not replace Question 39.
refined_question: Let d >= 3 and let f in Aut(C^d) be a polynomial automorphism. Write deg(f^n) for the polynomial degree of the n-th iterate and define the dynamical degree by lambda(f) := lim_{n->infinity} deg(f^n)^(1/n). Assume lambda(f) = 1. Must there exist an integer k >= 0 and constants c, C > 0 such that c n^k <= deg(f^n) <= C n^k for all sufficiently large n? Moreover, if k >= 1, must f preserve a rational fibration, i.e. is there a nonconstant dominant rational map pi: C^d -> B with 0 < dim(B) < d and a birational self-map g: B -> B such that pi o f = g o pi?
justification: The draft is targeting Section 10.1, Question 39, not a broader neighboring problem. The match is direct: the paper asks whether a polynomial automorphism f of C^d with lambda(f)=1 must satisfy deg(f^n) ~ n^k for some k in N, and whether the case k >= 1 forces preservation of a rational fibration (Section 10.1, Question 39, p. 23). The nearby context that must be imported for a stand-alone formulation is: (i) the higher-dimensional scope inherited from Problem 8, namely d >= 3 (Section 10.1, Problem 8, p. 23); (ii) the definition of lambda(f) via the limit of deg(f^n)^(1/n), established from submultiplicativity in the paragraph immediately preceding Question 39 (Section 10.1, p. 23); and (iii) the degree notation referenced back to Section 6.1 (Section 6.1, p. 14; Section 10.1, p. 23). The paragraph after Question 39 explicitly says that Question 40 is a weaker form of the same problem, so there is no paper-proved equivalent reformulation to supply (Section 10.1, Question 40, p. 23).
